mechanism: Thought to reduce pain and fever centrally in the brain and spinal cord; unlike NSAIDs it has little effect on inflammation
seriousSE: Liver damage in overdose or with heavy alcohol use
yellowing skin or eyes
warning: The most common cause of acute liver failure in overdose; check every other medicine for hidden acetaminophen before adding more
pregnancy: Considered safe at normal doses; the usual first choice in pregnancy

pill.strength: SODIUM STARCH GLYCOLATE TYPE A CORN 3.61 mg

mechanism: Blocks COX enzymes, reducing prostaglandins that cause pain, fever and inflammation
seriousSE: GI bleeding, kidney injury, heart attack or stroke risk with long-term use
warning: Avoid in the third trimester of pregnancy; take with food; avoid combining with other NSAIDs
pregnancy: Avoid, especially from 20 weeks; discuss any use with a clinician

mechanism: Same COX-blocking mechanism as ibuprofen, longer acting
seriousSE: GI bleeding, kidney injury, cardiovascular risk
warning: Longer half-life means effects and side effects last longer per dose
pregnancy: Avoid, especially from 20 weeks

uses: Pain, fever, and at low dose, clot prevention
mechanism: Blocks COX-1 irreversibly; at low doses this mainly stops platelets clumping
commonSE: Stomach upset, ringing in ears at high dose
seriousSE: GI bleeding, Reye syndrome in children with viral illness
warning: Never give to children or teenagers with a fever from a virus
pregnancy: Avoid for pain/fever in pregnancy; low-dose use only on medical advice

mechanism: A COX-2-selective NSAID, sparing the COX-1 enzyme that protects the stomach lining
seriousSE: Heart attack or stroke risk, GI bleeding (lower than older NSAIDs but not zero)
warning: Carries the same cardiovascular warning as other NSAIDs
pregnancy: Avoid, especially from 20 weeks

mechanism: COX-blocking NSAID; the gel/patch act mostly at the skin and joint below it
seriousSE: GI bleeding, liver enzyme changes, cardiovascular risk
warning: Topical forms have far lower whole-body exposure than tablets
pregnancy: Avoid oral form, especially from 20 weeks

mechanism: A weak opioid plus blocks reuptake of serotonin and noradrenaline
seriousSE: Seizures, serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs, dependence
warning: Lowers seizure threshold; dangerous with SSRIs/SNRIs/MAOIs due to serotonin syndrome risk
pregnancy: Can cause withdrawal in the newborn; discuss with a clinician

mechanism: A prodrug converted to morphine by the liver enzyme CYP2D6, which varies hugely between people
seriousSE: Severe breathing depression in people who convert it unusually fast (ultra-rapid metabolisers), especially children
warning: Not recommended for children after tonsillectomy; ultra-rapid metabolism can be fatal in breastfed infants
pregnancy: Avoid regular use; discuss with a clinician

mechanism: A full opioid agonist acting on mu-opioid receptors in the brain and spinal cord
seriousSE: Respiratory depression, overdose death, dependence
warning: Tolerance and dependence develop with regular use; naloxone reverses an overdose
pregnancy: Chronic use can cause neonatal withdrawal; use only as directed

mechanism: Full opioid agonist, similar to morphine but taken orally with reliable absorption
seriousSE: Respiratory depression, overdose death, dependence, diversion/misuse
warning: One of the most diverted prescription opioids; store securely and dispose of unused tablets
pregnancy: Chronic use can cause neonatal withdrawal

uses: Moderate to severe pain, cough (older combinations)
mechanism: Full opioid agonist similar to oxycodone
seriousSE: Respiratory depression, overdose death, dependence
warning: Combination products with acetaminophen add a liver-injury risk on top of the opioid risk
pregnancy: Chronic use can cause neonatal withdrawal

uses: Severe pain, including cancer pain and anaesthesia
mechanism: A very potent synthetic opioid, roughly 50-100 times morphine by weight
seriousSE: Fatal respiratory depression, especially if a patch is heated or in anyone opioid-naive
warning: The leading driver of fatal opioid overdoses when diverted into illicit drugs; a used patch still contains active drug
pregnancy: Specialist use only

mechanism: Binds a calcium channel subunit in nerves, calming overactive pain and seizure signalling
seriousSE: Breathing problems if combined with opioids, suicidal thoughts (rare)
warning: Increasingly misused in combination with opioids, which raises overdose risk
pregnancy: Discuss with a clinician

pill.manufacturer: McKesson Packaging Services a business unit of McKesson Corporation

uses: Ear, throat, sinus and chest infections, dental infections
mechanism: A penicillin that blocks bacteria from building their cell wall, causing them to burst
seriousSE: Severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis), Clostridioides difficile colitis
warning: Common allergy; a mild rash in a child with a viral illness is often mistaken for amoxicillin allergy
pregnancy: Generally considered safe in pregnancy

uses: Infections resistant to amoxicillin alone, including some skin and bite infections
mechanism: Adds clavulanate, which blocks the bacterial enzyme that would otherwise destroy amoxicillin
seriousSE: Liver injury (uncommon), severe allergic reaction
warning: Take with food to reduce stomach upset
pregnancy: Generally considered safe in pregnancy

mechanism: Blocks bacterial cell-wall synthesis
seriousSE: Anaphylaxis
warning: Poor absorption if taken with food; take on an empty stomach
pregnancy: Considered safe in pregnancy

uses: Skin, urinary tract and respiratory infections
mechanism: A cephalosporin, structurally related to penicillins, blocking cell-wall synthesis
seriousSE: Allergic reaction (some cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy)
warning: Cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy is lower than once thought but still possible
pregnancy: Generally considered safe in pregnancy

mechanism: A broad-spectrum injectable cephalosporin
seriousSE: Allergic reaction, gallbladder sludge
warning: Given by injection or IV, usually in hospital or clinic
pregnancy: Generally considered safe in pregnancy

uses: Respiratory and some sexually transmitted infections
mechanism: A macrolide that blocks bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome
seriousSE: Heart rhythm changes (QT prolongation), rare liver injury
warning: Can prolong the QT interval; caution with other QT-prolonging drugs
pregnancy: Generally considered safe in pregnancy

uses: Respiratory infections, H. pylori (with other drugs)
mechanism: Macrolide, blocks bacterial protein synthesis
seriousSE: QT prolongation, many drug interactions via liver enzymes
warning: Interacts with a long list of other drugs through CYP3A4
pregnancy: Caution; alternatives often preferred

uses: Acne, respiratory infections, Lyme disease, malaria prevention
mechanism: A tetracycline that blocks bacterial protein synthesis
seriousSE: Permanent tooth discolouration in children, rare liver or intracranial pressure effects
warning: Take with plenty of water sitting upright; avoid in children under 8 and in pregnancy
pregnancy: Avoid; can discolour the baby’s developing teeth

uses: Urinary tract, some gut and respiratory infections
mechanism: A fluoroquinolone that blocks bacterial DNA-copying enzymes
seriousSE: Tendon rupture, nerve damage, aortic aneurysm risk, QT prolongation
warning: Carries a boxed warning for tendon and nerve damage; reserved for when other antibiotics will not do
pregnancy: Generally avoided unless no alternative

uses: Pneumonia, urinary tract and sinus infections
mechanism: Fluoroquinolone, same mechanism and warnings as ciprofloxacin
seriousSE: Tendon rupture, nerve damage, QT prolongation
warning: Same boxed warnings as other fluoroquinolones
pregnancy: Generally avoided unless no alternative

uses: Urinary tract infections, some skin and respiratory infections
mechanism: Blocks two sequential steps in bacterial folate synthesis
seriousSE: Severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), blood count drops, high potassium
warning: Contains a sulfa drug; avoid in sulfa allergy
pregnancy: Avoid near term; can affect newborn bilirubin handling

uses: Certain gut, pelvic and dental infections, some parasites
mechanism: Damages the DNA of anaerobic bacteria and some parasites
seriousSE: Peripheral nerve damage with prolonged use
warning: Avoid alcohol during and for days after treatment: causes a severe flushing reaction
pregnancy: Generally considered acceptable after the first trimester on medical advice

uses: Skin and soft-tissue infections, some dental and pelvic infections, acne (topical)
mechanism: Blocks bacterial protein synthesis
seriousSE: Clostridioides difficile colitis (notably higher risk than most antibiotics)
warning: One of the antibiotics most strongly linked to C. difficile diarrhoea
pregnancy: Generally considered acceptable

uses: Serious resistant infections (IV); C. difficile colitis (oral)
mechanism: Blocks cell-wall building in a different way from penicillins, including resistant bacteria
commonSE: Flushing (“red man syndrome” with fast infusion), nausea
seriousSE: Kidney injury, hearing loss at high levels
warning: Blood levels are monitored to keep dosing safe and effective
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: Damages bacterial DNA and proteins; concentrates in urine
seriousSE: Lung and liver injury with long-term use, blood cell breakdown in G6PD deficiency
warning: Avoid near term in pregnancy and in G6PD deficiency
pregnancy: Avoid at term (38-42 weeks)

mechanism: Blocks bacterial RNA synthesis
seriousSE: Liver injury
warning: Turns urine, sweat and tears orange-red (harmless but alarming); induces many drug-metabolising enzymes, reducing the effect of other drugs including the contraceptive pill
pregnancy: Used in pregnancy when TB treatment is needed

mechanism: Blocks mycobacterial cell-wall (mycolic acid) synthesis
seriousSE: Liver injury, peripheral neuropathy
warning: Vitamin B6 is usually given alongside it to prevent nerve damage
pregnancy: Used in pregnancy when TB treatment is needed

mechanism: Blocks the viral enzyme neuraminidase, stopping new flu virus particles from leaving infected cells
seriousSE: Rare neuropsychiatric events (confusion, self-injury), mostly reported in children in Japan
warning: Most effective when started within 48 hours of symptoms
pregnancy: Generally considered acceptable when flu treatment is needed

uses: Herpes simplex (cold sores, genital herpes), chickenpox, shingles
mechanism: Blocks viral DNA synthesis in infected cells
seriousSE: Kidney injury at high IV doses if not well hydrated
warning: Does not cure herpes; it shortens and lessens outbreaks and can be used for suppression
pregnancy: Generally considered safe

mechanism: A prodrug that converts to acyclovir with better absorption, allowing less frequent dosing
seriousSE: Rare kidney or blood effects at high doses
warning: Starting within 72 hours of a shingles rash gives the best effect
pregnancy: Generally considered safe

mechanism: Two reverse transcriptase inhibitors that block HIV from copying its genetic material
seriousSE: Kidney effects, bone density loss (tenofovir DF)
warning: As PrEP it is highly effective at preventing HIV when taken consistently
pregnancy: Used in pregnancy to prevent mother-to-child transmission

uses: Yeast infections (vaginal, oral thrush, some systemic)
mechanism: Blocks an enzyme fungi need to build their cell membrane
seriousSE: Liver injury, QT prolongation, many drug interactions
warning: A single dose treats most vaginal yeast infections
pregnancy: Avoid high-dose use in pregnancy; single low dose use varies by guideline

uses: Athlete’s foot, ringworm, vaginal yeast infections, oral thrush
mechanism: Same antifungal mechanism as fluconazole, applied topically
seriousSE: Rare allergic reaction
warning: Topical use means very little reaches the rest of the body
pregnancy: Considered safe

uses: Fungal nail infections, athlete’s foot, ringworm
mechanism: Blocks a different step of fungal membrane building than azoles
seriousSE: Liver injury (oral form)
warning: Oral courses for nail infections run for weeks to months; liver function is sometimes checked
pregnancy: Avoid oral form; topical generally considered lower risk

uses: High blood pressure, heart failure, after heart attack
mechanism: An ACE inhibitor that blocks the enzyme making angiotensin II, relaxing blood vessels
seriousSE: High potassium, kidney function changes, angioedema (swelling of lips/throat)
warning: Stop and seek care immediately for facial or throat swelling
pregnancy: Avoid, especially after the first trimester: can harm fetal kidneys

mechanism: ACE inhibitor, same mechanism as lisinopril
seriousSE: High potassium, angioedema, kidney effects
warning: Same class warnings as lisinopril
pregnancy: Avoid, especially after the first trimester

uses: High blood pressure, kidney protection in diabetes
mechanism: An ARB that blocks angiotensin II at its receptor instead of blocking its production
seriousSE: Kidney function changes, rare angioedema
warning: Less cough than ACE inhibitors because it does not affect the pathway that causes it
pregnancy: Avoid, especially after the first trimester

mechanism: ARB, same mechanism as losartan
seriousSE: Kidney function changes
warning: Often combined with a diuretic in one tablet
pregnancy: Avoid, especially after the first trimester

mechanism: A calcium channel blocker that relaxes blood vessel walls
seriousSE: Low blood pressure, rarely worsened heart failure
warning: Ankle swelling is common and not dangerous, but can prompt people to stop taking it
pregnancy: Generally considered acceptable when needed

uses: High blood pressure, angina, some arrhythmias
mechanism: Calcium channel blocker that also slows the heart’s electrical conduction
seriousSE: Very slow heart rate, heart block
warning: Should not be combined with a beta blocker without specialist advice because both slow the heart
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

uses: High blood pressure, angina, after heart attack, arrhythmias
mechanism: A beta blocker that reduces the heart’s response to adrenaline, slowing and steadying it
seriousSE: Very slow heart rate, worsened asthma, masking low blood sugar symptoms
warning: Never stop abruptly: can trigger rebound high blood pressure or chest pain
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk; newborn may need monitoring

mechanism: Beta blocker, similar to metoprolol
seriousSE: Very slow heart rate, worsened asthma
warning: Same “do not stop abruptly” rule as other beta blockers
pregnancy: Generally avoided; other beta blockers preferred

mechanism: A beta blocker that also blocks alpha receptors, relaxing vessels as well as slowing the heart
seriousSE: Worsened heart failure if started too high, very slow heart rate
warning: Started at a very low dose and increased slowly in heart failure
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: A thiazide diuretic that increases salt and water loss by the kidney
seriousSE: Low sodium, gout flares, raised blood sugar
warning: Often combined with other blood pressure medicines in one tablet
pregnancy: Generally avoided near delivery

uses: Fluid overload, heart failure, kidney disease
mechanism: A loop diuretic, a stronger and faster-acting water pill than thiazides
seriousSE: Low sodium/potassium, hearing changes at high IV doses, kidney injury if over-diuresed
warning: Weigh daily if on it for heart failure; a sudden weight gain can mean fluid is building up again
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

uses: Heart failure, fluid retention, high blood pressure, acne/hormonal uses
mechanism: A potassium-sparing diuretic that blocks aldosterone
commonSE: Breast tenderness (can affect any sex), increased urination
seriousSE: High potassium, especially with ACE inhibitors or ARBs
warning: Potassium is checked regularly when combined with an ACE inhibitor or ARB
pregnancy: Generally avoided; can have anti-androgen effects on a male fetus

mechanism: Blocks HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in liver cholesterol production
commonSE: Muscle aches, mild liver enzyme rise
seriousSE: Severe muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis, rare), liver injury
warning: Report unexplained muscle pain, especially with dark urine
pregnancy: Avoid; cholesterol synthesis matters for fetal development

mechanism: Statin, same mechanism as atorvastatin, more potent per milligram
seriousSE: Rhabdomyolysis (rare), liver injury
warning: Same muscle-pain warning as other statins
pregnancy: Avoid

mechanism: Statin, same mechanism
commonSE: Muscle aches, mild liver enzyme rise
seriousSE: Rhabdomyolysis, especially at high doses or with interacting drugs
warning: Grapefruit juice and several other drugs raise simvastatin levels and muscle-damage risk
pregnancy: Avoid

uses: Preventing clots after stent placement, heart attack or stroke
mechanism: An antiplatelet that blocks a receptor platelets use to clump together
seriousSE: Serious bleeding, rare blood disorder (TTP)
warning: Often paired with aspirin for a set period after a cardiac stent; stopping early can risk the stent clotting
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

uses: Preventing and treating blood clots, atrial fibrillation, mechanical heart valves
mechanism: Blocks the liver’s use of vitamin K to make clotting factors
seriousSE: Major bleeding, especially with missed monitoring or drug/diet interactions
warning: Blood level (INR) must be checked regularly; vitamin K intake should be kept consistent, not avoided
pregnancy: Avoid in the first trimester (birth defects); used with caution later if essential

uses: Preventing and treating blood clots, atrial fibrillation
mechanism: A direct factor Xa inhibitor, blocking one clotting-cascade step without needing monitoring
seriousSE: Major bleeding
no routine reversal agent in some settings (specific reversal agents exist)
warning: No regular blood monitoring needed, unlike warfarin, but missed doses matter more
pregnancy: Limited data; usually avoided

uses: Preventing and treating blood clots, atrial fibrillation
mechanism: Direct factor Xa inhibitor, same class as apixaban
seriousSE: Major bleeding
warning: Take with food for the higher-dose tablet to ensure full absorption
pregnancy: Limited data; usually avoided

uses: Heart failure, atrial fibrillation rate control
mechanism: Increases the force of heart muscle contraction and slows conduction through the AV node
seriousSE: Digoxin toxicity: nausea, confusion, dangerous arrhythmias, especially with low potassium
warning: Narrow safety margin; blood levels and potassium are monitored
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

pill.manufacturer: Amneal Pharmaceuticals of New York LLC

mechanism: Blocks multiple cardiac ion channels, broadly slowing abnormal electrical activity
seriousSE: Lung scarring, thyroid dysfunction, liver injury, corneal deposits
warning: One of the few drugs that needs regular lung, thyroid, liver and eye checks during long-term use
pregnancy: Can affect fetal thyroid function; used only when essential

mechanism: Reduces glucose production by the liver and improves insulin sensitivity
seriousSE: Lactic acidosis (rare, mainly with kidney failure), vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use
warning: Usually the first medicine tried for type 2 diabetes; stopped temporarily before contrast dye scans in some cases
pregnancy: Often continued; considered reasonable in pregnancy/PCOS on medical advice

mechanism: A sulfonylurea that makes the pancreas release more insulin
seriousSE: Severe hypoglycaemia, especially if a meal is skipped

pregnancy: Usually switched to insulin in pregnancy

mechanism: Sulfonylurea, same mechanism, longer-acting
seriousSE: Severe hypoglycaemia
warning: Longer action means hypoglycaemia can occur later and last longer
pregnancy: Usually switched to insulin in pregnancy

mechanism: A DPP-4 inhibitor that prolongs the body’s own incretin hormones, boosting insulin after meals
seriousSE: Pancreatitis (rare), joint pain
warning: Low risk of hypoglycaemia on its own
pregnancy: Limited data; insulin usually preferred

uses: Type 2 diabetes, heart failure, kidney protection

seriousSE: Diabetic ketoacidosis with normal blood sugar (rare), dehydration, rare serious genital infection

pregnancy: Not recommended; insulin usually preferred

uses: Type 2 diabetes, heart failure, kidney protection
mechanism: SGLT2 inhibitor, same mechanism as empagliflozin
seriousSE: Ketoacidosis, dehydration
warning: Same pause-before-surgery caution as other SGLT2 inhibitors
pregnancy: Not recommended

mechanism: A GLP-1 receptor agonist that boosts insulin, slows stomach emptying and reduces appetite
seriousSE: Pancreatitis (rare), gallbladder disease, possible thyroid C-cell tumours in animal studies
warning: Not for people with a personal or family history of certain thyroid cancers
pregnancy: Not recommended; stop before a planned pregnancy

mechanism: GLP-1 receptor agonist, same mechanism as semaglutide, taken daily
seriousSE: Pancreatitis, gallbladder disease
warning: Same thyroid-tumour caution as other GLP-1 drugs
pregnancy: Not recommended

mechanism: A long-acting insulin analogue giving a steady background level over about 24 hours
commonSE: Low blood sugar, injection site reactions
seriousSE: Severe hypoglycaemia
warning: Does not need to be timed with meals, unlike fast-acting insulin
pregnancy: Insulin is the preferred diabetes treatment in pregnancy

uses: Type 1 and type 2 diabetes, mealtime control

seriousSE: Severe hypoglycaemia
warning: Taken shortly before eating; timing matters more than with long-acting insulin
pregnancy: Preferred diabetes treatment in pregnancy

mechanism: An intermediate-acting insulin with a cloudy suspension and a pronounced peak

seriousSE: Severe hypoglycaemia, especially at its peak action

pregnancy: Used in pregnancy when appropriate

mechanism: A thiazolidinedione that improves insulin sensitivity in fat and muscle
seriousSE: Heart failure, bone fracture risk, bladder cancer signal (debated)

pregnancy: Not recommended; insulin preferred

pregnancy: Often continued when benefit outweighs risk; discuss with a clinician

mechanism: SSRI, closely related to citalopram
seriousSE: Serotonin syndrome, QT prolongation at high doses, suicidal thoughts in young people early on
warning: One of the better-tolerated SSRIs in terms of drug interactions
pregnancy: Often continued when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: SSRI with an unusually long half-life, so it tapers itself off slowly
seriousSE: Serotonin syndrome, suicidal thoughts in young people early on

pregnancy: Often continued when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: An SNRI that blocks reuptake of both serotonin and noradrenaline
commonSE: Nausea, sweating, raised blood pressure at higher doses
seriousSE: Serotonin syndrome, severe withdrawal if stopped abruptly, raised blood pressure
warning: Known for a difficult discontinuation syndrome; taper slowly under supervision
pregnancy: Often continued when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: SNRI, similar mechanism to venlafaxine
seriousSE: Serotonin syndrome, liver injury (rare), withdrawal symptoms
warning: Also used for chronic pain conditions, not only mood
pregnancy: Often continued when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: Blocks reuptake of dopamine and noradrenaline; does not act on serotonin
seriousSE: Seizures at high doses or in people prone to them
warning: Avoid in anyone with a seizure disorder or eating disorder, which raise seizure risk further
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

uses: Depression, especially with poor sleep or appetite
mechanism: Increases noradrenaline and serotonin release by a different receptor mechanism; sedating
commonSE: Drowsiness, increased appetite and weight gain
seriousSE: Low white blood cell count (rare)

pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

uses: Depression (less common now), nerve pain, migraine prevention

mechanism: Blocks serotonin receptors and reuptake; sedating at lower doses
seriousSE: Priapism (prolonged painful erection, rare), low blood pressure

mechanism: A non-benzodiazepine anxiolytic acting on serotonin receptors, with no sedation or dependence
seriousSE: Serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs (rare)

mechanism: Benzodiazepine, same mechanism as alprazolam

uses: Anxiety, muscle spasm, seizures, alcohol withdrawal

uses: Schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, irritability in autism

pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

uses: Schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression (adjunct), off-label for sleep

mechanism: A partial dopamine agonist, a different mechanism from most other antipsychotics

pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: A typical (first-generation) antipsychotic, strongly blocking dopamine receptors
seriousSE: Tardive dyskinesia, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, QT prolongation

pregnancy: Small increase in heart defect risk; used when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: Thought to enhance GABA and stabilise neuronal firing

pregnancy: Avoid: one of the highest-risk drugs for birth defects and developmental problems

mechanism: Stabilises neuronal sodium channels, calming overactive firing

pregnancy: Often continued when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: A stimulant that increases dopamine and noradrenaline availability, improving focus

pregnancy: Limited data; discuss risks and benefits with a clinician

mechanism: A stimulant combination increasing dopamine and noradrenaline, similar effect to methylphenidate
commonSE: Decreased appetite, insomnia, increased heart rate
seriousSE: Cardiovascular risk, growth suppression in children, misuse and dependence potential
warning: Widely misused as a study aid; use outside a prescription carries real cardiovascular and dependence risk
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk; can cause low birth weight

pill.manufacturer: Global Pharmaceuticals, Division of Impax Laboratories Inc.

seriousSE: Cardiovascular risk, growth suppression, psychiatric symptoms at high doses

pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

uses: Asthma and COPD symptom relief, acute wheeze

uses: Asthma and COPD maintenance (and some reliever regimens)

pregnancy: Considered safe when used as directed

mechanism: A long-acting anticholinergic that relaxes airway muscle by a different pathway
seriousSE: Urinary retention, worsening glaucoma (rare)

pregnancy: Limited data; used when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: Blocks leukotriene receptors, reducing allergic airway inflammation

mechanism: Second-generation antihistamine, similar to cetirizine, usually non-drowsy

seriousSE: Confusion in older adults, anticholinergic toxicity in overdose
warning: Not recommended for regular sleep use or in older adults because of fall and confusion risk
pregnancy: Occasional use generally considered acceptable

mechanism: Second-generation antihistamine, non-drowsy
seriousSE: Rare allergic reaction
warning: Should be taken apart from fruit juices, which can reduce its absorption
pregnancy: Considered acceptable

mechanism: A decongestant that narrows blood vessels in the nasal lining, reducing swelling
seriousSE: Dangerously high blood pressure, heart rhythm effects in susceptible people
warning: Sold from behind the pharmacy counter in many countries because it is a precursor for illicit drug manufacture
pregnancy: Caution, especially in the first trimester

mechanism: Activates adrenaline receptors throughout the body: opens airways, raises blood pressure, reduces swelling
seriousSE: Dangerous arrhythmia (rare, and far outweighed by the risk of untreated anaphylaxis)
warning: Always call emergency services after use, even if symptoms improve: a second wave (biphasic reaction) can follow
pregnancy: Use immediately regardless of pregnancy: untreated anaphylaxis is the greater danger

uses: Acid reflux, ulcers, H. pylori treatment (with antibiotics)
mechanism: A proton pump inhibitor that blocks the stomach’s acid-producing pump
seriousSE: Low magnesium, increased fracture risk, kidney disease and nutrient deficiencies with long-term use
warning: Long-term use is now linked to several slow-building risks; periodic review of ongoing need is reasonable
pregnancy: Considered acceptable when needed

mechanism: Proton pump inhibitor, closely related to omeprazole
seriousSE: Same long-term risks as omeprazole
warning: Same class cautions as omeprazole
pregnancy: Considered acceptable when needed

uses: Acid reflux, ulcers, stress ulcer prevention in hospital
mechanism: Proton pump inhibitor
seriousSE: Same long-term risks as other PPIs
warning: Commonly used by injection in hospitalised patients
pregnancy: Considered acceptable when needed

mechanism: An H2 blocker that reduces acid production by a different pathway than PPIs
seriousSE: Contamination with a probable carcinogen (NDMA) led most original ranitidine products to be withdrawn
reformulated versions use a different active ingredient
warning: Check which active ingredient a “Zantac” product actually contains before assuming it is the original drug
pregnancy: Check current product composition

mechanism: H2 blocker, same mechanism as the original ranitidine, not affected by its contamination issue
seriousSE: Rare confusion in older adults, especially at high doses or with kidney impairment
warning: Became the main H2 blocker in use after ranitidine’s withdrawal
pregnancy: Considered acceptable when needed

uses: Nausea and vomiting, including from chemotherapy and pregnancy
mechanism: Blocks serotonin (5-HT3) receptors in the gut and brainstem that trigger vomiting
seriousSE: QT prolongation at high doses, serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs
warning: Used widely for severe pregnancy nausea, though data on fetal risk are still debated
pregnancy: Commonly used for severe nausea; discuss with a clinician

mechanism: Blocks dopamine receptors in the gut and brain and speeds stomach emptying
seriousSE: Movement disorders (tardive dyskinesia) with prolonged use (boxed warning)
warning: Carries a boxed warning against use for more than 12 weeks because of the movement-disorder risk
pregnancy: Used short-term when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: An opioid-receptor drug that acts only in the gut at normal doses, slowing transit
seriousSE: Dangerous heart rhythm changes at very high (misused) doses
warning: Misusing very high doses to get an opioid-like effect has caused fatal heart rhythm problems
pregnancy: Considered acceptable for short-term use

mechanism: Lets water and fat mix into the stool, softening it
seriousSE: None significant
warning: One of the gentlest laxatives, often used to prevent straining rather than treat established constipation
pregnancy: Considered safe

mechanism: A stimulant laxative that triggers gut muscle contractions
seriousSE: Electrolyte loss, “lazy bowel” with chronic overuse
warning: Not meant for daily long-term use without medical advice
pregnancy: Considered acceptable for short-term use

mechanism: An osmotic laxative that holds water in the stool
seriousSE: Electrolyte disturbance with excessive use
warning: Often the first choice for ongoing constipation because it is gentle and not habit forming
pregnancy: Considered safe

mechanism: A synthetic form of the thyroid hormone T4, replacing what the gland is not making
commonSE: symptoms of too much thyroid hormone if overdosed (palpitations, weight loss)
seriousSE: Heart rhythm problems and bone loss if persistently overdosed
warning: Take on an empty stomach, apart from calcium, iron and coffee, which reduce absorption
pregnancy: Essential in pregnancy; dose usually needs increasing

mechanism: Blocks the thyroid gland’s ability to make thyroid hormone
seriousSE: Low white blood cell count (agranulocytosis, rare but serious), liver injury
warning: Seek care urgently for fever or sore throat, which can signal the rare blood count drop
pregnancy: Avoid in the first trimester if possible; alternative used instead

uses: Inflammation, autoimmune disease, allergic reactions, asthma flares
mechanism: A corticosteroid that broadly suppresses the immune system and inflammation
commonSE: Increased appetite, mood changes, insomnia, raised blood sugar
seriousSE: Adrenal suppression with long courses, osteoporosis, increased infection risk, stomach ulcers
warning: Do not stop a long course abruptly: the adrenal glands need time to resume their own production
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: Corticosteroid, same family as prednisone; topical forms act mainly on the skin
commonSE: Topical: skin thinning with overuse. Oral: see prednisone
seriousSE: Oral: adrenal suppression, infection risk. Topical: skin thinning with prolonged use on the face
warning: Topical steroids are graded by strength; the mildest effective strength should be used, especially on the face
pregnancy: Topical considered safe; oral used when benefit outweighs risk

uses: Contraception, cycle regulation, acne, endometriosis symptoms
mechanism: Oestrogen and progestin together suppress ovulation
seriousSE: Blood clots (DVT/PE), stroke risk increase in smokers over 35 or with migraine with aura
warning: Avoid in smokers over 35 and in anyone with migraine with aura because of the stroke-risk interaction
pregnancy: Not used during pregnancy; stopped once pregnancy is confirmed

mechanism: A progestin alone, thickening cervical mucus and partly suppressing ovulation
seriousSE: Lower clot risk than combined pills but not zero
warning: Must be taken at the same time each day more strictly than combined pills
pregnancy: Not used during pregnancy

mechanism: Replaces testosterone to normal male physiological levels
commonSE: Acne, mood changes, increased red blood cell count
seriousSE: Blood clots, worsened sleep apnoea, fertility suppression, cardiovascular risk debate
warning: Gel forms can transfer to others by skin contact; cover the area after application
pregnancy: Not applicable

mechanism: A bisphosphonate that slows bone breakdown by osteoclasts
seriousSE: Oesophageal ulceration if lying down too soon after taking it, rare jaw bone death, rare atypical fractures with long-term use
warning: Must be taken with a full glass of water, sitting or standing upright for at least 30 minutes afterward
pregnancy: Generally avoided; long bone half-life means past use can matter too

mechanism: Binds a synaptic vesicle protein, reducing abnormal neuronal firing by a mechanism unlike older anti-seizure drugs
seriousSE: Rare severe mood or behavioural change, psychosis (uncommon)
warning: Fewer drug interactions than many older anti-seizure medicines, which is why it is now widely used
pregnancy: Generally considered one of the better-studied options in pregnancy

mechanism: Stabilises neuronal sodium channels
seriousSE: Severe skin reactions, liver injury, toxicity with a narrow safety margin
warning: Blood levels are monitored closely; small dose changes can have large effects at higher levels
pregnancy: Associated with a recognised pattern of birth defects (fetal hydantoin syndrome); used when necessary

mechanism: Stabilises sodium channels, similar effect to phenytoin
seriousSE: Severe skin reactions (higher risk in people with a specific HLA gene variant, tested for in some ethnicities), low blood counts
warning: A genetic test (HLA-B*1502) is recommended in some populations before starting, to screen for severe rash risk
pregnancy: Associated with neural tube and other defects; folic acid supplementation is important

uses: Seizures (also used for bipolar disorder, see Mental health)
mechanism: Stabilises sodium channels
seriousSE: Severe skin reactions if the dose is increased too quickly
warning: See the Mental health entry for the same drug used for mood
pregnancy: Often continued; dose may need adjusting in pregnancy

mechanism: Multiple actions including sodium channel and GABA effects
commonSE: Tingling in fingers/toes, word-finding difficulty, weight loss
seriousSE: Kidney stones, acute glaucoma, metabolic acidosis, birth defects (cleft lip/palate)
warning: Known for causing word-finding and concentration problems, sometimes called “Dopamax” by patients
pregnancy: Avoid if possible: clear link to cleft lip and palate

mechanism: A triptan that narrows blood vessels in the brain and blocks pain-signal release via serotonin receptors
seriousSE: Heart attack or stroke risk in people with cardiovascular disease (contraindicated)
warning: Not for anyone with uncontrolled high blood pressure or known cardiovascular disease
pregnancy: Limited data; used when migraine is severe and other options fail

uses: Migraine prevention, tremor, anxiety symptoms, high blood pressure
mechanism: A non-selective beta blocker; for migraine the mechanism is not fully understood
commonSE: Fatigue, cold hands, slow heart rate
seriousSE: Worsened asthma, very slow heart rate, masking low blood sugar symptoms
warning: Avoid in asthma because non-selective beta blockade can trigger bronchospasm
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: A retinoid (vitamin A derivative) that speeds skin cell turnover and unclogs pores
seriousSE: Severe irritation if overused
birth defects if taken orally (not used orally for acne)
warning: Use at night and always wear sunscreen by day: it markedly increases sun sensitivity
pregnancy: Avoid: oral retinoids are a well-known cause of birth defects, and topical use is avoided as a precaution

mechanism: Kills acne-causing bacteria and helps unclog pores
commonSE: Dryness, bleaching of fabric and hair
seriousSE: Severe allergic reaction (rare)
warning: Can bleach towels, pillowcases and clothing; use white linens or apply carefully
pregnancy: Considered acceptable

mechanism: A mild topical corticosteroid reducing local inflammation and itching
seriousSE: Skin thinning, stretch marks with overuse, especially on the face or skin folds
warning: The mildest available steroid strength, reasonable for short-term use on most body areas
pregnancy: Considered safe for short-term use

mechanism: A potent topical corticosteroid
seriousSE: Significant skin thinning and systemic absorption with overuse on large areas or under occlusion
warning: A high-potency steroid: avoid the face and skin folds, and avoid prolonged continuous use
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk, with caution

mechanism: A neurotoxin to mites and lice that is poorly absorbed through human skin
seriousSE: Rare allergic reaction
warning: Itching can continue for 1-2 weeks after successful treatment as dead mites clear; this is not treatment failure
pregnancy: Considered acceptable

mechanism: A prostaglandin analogue that increases drainage of fluid from the eye
commonSE: Eye redness, eyelash growth, iris colour darkening (if long-term)
seriousSE: Rare systemic effects are unusual because so little drug is absorbed
warning: Can permanently darken light-coloured eyes over months to years of use
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: A beta blocker that reduces fluid production inside the eye
seriousSE: Can be absorbed enough to slow the heart or worsen asthma in susceptible people
warning: Press on the inner corner of the eye after applying to reduce drainage into the bloodstream
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: Same fluoroquinolone mechanism as the oral form, applied locally
seriousSE: Minimal systemic absorption at normal use
warning: Local use carries far less of the tendon/nerve risk associated with oral fluoroquinolones
pregnancy: Considered low risk topically

uses: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, some cancers, ectopic pregnancy treatment
mechanism: Blocks folate metabolism, slowing rapidly dividing cells (immune cells at low dose, cancer cells at high dose)
seriousSE: Liver injury, low blood counts, lung inflammation
fatal overdose if daily dosing is mistaken for weekly dosing
warning: For arthritis it is taken weekly, not daily; dosing errors (daily instead of weekly) have caused deaths
pregnancy: Avoid: a known cause of major birth defects and pregnancy loss

mechanism: Modifies immune cell activity inside cells; the exact anti-inflammatory mechanism is not fully clear
seriousSE: Retinal damage with long-term high-dose use (regular eye exams needed)
warning: Annual eye exams are recommended to catch early retinal toxicity before vision is affected
pregnancy: Generally continued in lupus/pregnancy on medical advice

uses: Rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn’s disease, psoriasis, and others
mechanism: A TNF-inhibitor biologic that blocks a key inflammatory signalling protein
seriousSE: Serious infection (including reactivated TB), rare lymphoma signal, worsened heart failure
warning: Screened for latent TB and hepatitis B before starting, because TNF blockade can let them reactivate
pregnancy: Often continued when benefit outweighs risk, per specialist advice

uses: Same uses as prednisone (the two are closely related and often interchangeable)
mechanism: Corticosteroid, see prednisone
seriousSE: Adrenal suppression, osteoporosis, infection risk with long courses
warning: Prednisolone is the active form the liver converts prednisone into; used directly in liver disease or young children
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

mechanism: Blocks oestrogen receptors in breast tissue while having oestrogen-like effects elsewhere
seriousSE: Blood clots, increased risk of uterine cancer, stroke
warning: Report any unusual vaginal bleeding promptly because of the uterine cancer association
pregnancy: Avoid: can harm the fetus and is used during active cancer treatment, where pregnancy is generally avoided

uses: Chemotherapy-induced nausea (see also Stomach and gut)
mechanism: See the Stomach and gut entry for the same drug
seriousSE: QT prolongation at high doses
warning: Often given before chemotherapy starts, pre-emptively rather than after nausea begins
pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk

uses: Low blood potassium, often alongside certain diuretics
mechanism: Directly replaces potassium lost through the kidneys or gut
seriousSE: Dangerously high potassium if overdosed or combined with potassium-sparing diuretics/ACE inhibitors
warning: Extended-release tablets must be swallowed whole, not crushed, to avoid releasing too much at once
pregnancy: Used when a genuine deficiency is confirmed

mechanism: Replenishes iron stores needed to make haemoglobin
seriousSE: Iron overdose is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in young children who find the tablets
warning: Keep iron tablets locked away from children: even a modest number of adult tablets can be fatal to a toddler
pregnancy: Often specifically recommended in pregnancy for anaemia

mechanism: Restores the hormone needed for calcium absorption and bone health
seriousSE: Hypercalcaemia (high blood calcium) if grossly overdosed
warning: High-dose prescription courses are time-limited, then switched to a lower maintenance dose
pregnancy: Standard doses considered safe; discuss higher doses with a clinician

uses: Folate deficiency, prevention of neural tube defects
mechanism: Replenishes folate, needed for DNA synthesis and red blood cell formation
seriousSE: Can mask vitamin B12 deficiency if taken without checking B12
warning: Recommended before and during early pregnancy specifically to prevent spina bifida and related defects
pregnancy: Specifically recommended before and during early pregnancy

uses: Low magnesium, constipation, migraine prevention (some use)
mechanism: Replenishes magnesium, involved in hundreds of enzyme reactions
seriousSE: Dangerously high magnesium in kidney failure
warning: The most common side effect, loose stools, is also why some forms are sold as laxatives
pregnancy: Considered acceptable at normal doses
